fun_facts: It's named after a Miami taxidermist, not a scientist: Tetrapturus pfluegeri honors Al Pflueger Sr., whose shop mounted a huge share of the trophy billfish caught off Florida in the mid-20th century.

The species wasn't formally recognized as distinct from its Atlantic relatives until 1963 -- for decades, anglers and scientists alike had likely been calling occasional longbill spearfish catches something else entirely.

Slimmer than a marlin and carrying a sail lower than a sailfish's, the longbill spearfish is built more for a quick sprint than a long fight, and to this day it turns up almost entirely as bycatch rather than a species anyone sets out to catch.

measures.label: Lower jaw fork length
measures.help: Tip of the lower jaw to the fork of the tail, measured in a straight line -- the standard billfish measurement.

vocabs.label: Sex
vocabs.help: Longbill spearfish cannot be sexed externally in the field; unknown is the normal answer.

vocabs.label: Condition at release
vocabs.help: Billfish tagging is normally done boat-side, leaving the fish in the water where possible.

not_taggable.reason: a fish in poor condition or bleeding is unlikely to survive release, so tagging it wastes the tag and the reward

must_release.reason: longbill spearfish are a prohibited species under US Atlantic Highly Migratory Species regulations: retention is not legal under any circumstance; every longbill spearfish encountered in this tagging programme is released
